newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea length pressures CFDs, wet action stiffled.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea length pressures CFDs, wet action stiffled.

text.p: North Sea markets were mixed on Tuesday as paper levels generally fell off in active trade but some traders felt physical Brent had reached the bottom.
Following the earlier deal of an April 1-3 Brent at May Brent -80 cents the two sellers of April loading cargoes were heard offering on a dated related basis.
Although a VLCC has been fixed to travel with early April loading Brent to the U.S. Gulf, some expected the crude to move to South Africa.
Overall the sloppiness in the wet market continued and with U.S. Gulf buyers thin on the ground European-based traders expected only one ship to move transatlantic.
Brent CFDs recovered from the lows of the day with next weeks 31-04 talked at May -56/-52 cents, up from the lowest deal at May -60 cents.
The April/May Brent spread was worst hit, trading recently at -30 cents. May/June traded between -4 and -8 cents but fell back to talk around -10 cents.
In the Mediterranean traders said Brent at a notional May Brent -60/-80 cents looked on the verge of becoming competitive against other sweet grades.
But they added the grade would probably need a further 20-cent reduction in order to displace other grades in the region.
The market overall remains still long, weakened by oversupply bolstered by April Kirkuk flows and continuing refinery turnarounds.
